main_text.l: Orionis statura pro Gigatea ponitur, visu quidè concè-
ptibilis apparuit, sed indefessus in cogressu. Virtus etiâ in
exili corpore regnat, admonet hostè nullum tam esse hu-
milem, quem oporteat contemnere. vide prouerb. Habet
& musca splenem: &, Ineft etiam formicæ bilis.
Καίτοι πρὸς Ἀνταῖον.) Exemplū Herculis qui Antæo colla-

tura, tamen eum vicit. Hercules è Thebis profectus in Li-
byam, quæsiuit Antæum, qui craniis hospitum intefecto-
rum templum Neptuno construebat, eumque oppressit:
sic Melissus multò maiorem staturam hostem supera-
uit. Bacchylides Euenum hunc appellat: alij Diomedem
Thracem ea perpetrasse scribunt: Sophocles Oenomao
tribuit. Libya πυροφόρος[?] dicitur, quû magna parte solitudi-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the Greek tags at the start of the Οὐ γὰρ and Καίτοι paragraphs are read from a small, faint print and may be inexact. "πυροφόρος" is uncertain, the word is smudged. The second word of the verse line "Pectora fu..." is partly illegible; the visible letters are read as "fu". "Vlysse" is printed with a double-s ligature, transcribed as s. "cœloq" is partly unclear. Hyphens at line ends are printed and kept. The printed text contains "Viysse"-like spelling only as the ligature for Vlysse, and "Orioneam" and "Libyam" are as printed.
